subject: Intermittent large-packet failures after private cutover - urgent troubleshooting
messages:
From: Nora Singh <nora@acmetech.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmetech.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent large-packet failures after private cutover

Mina / Redwood team,

We completed the private VPC peering cutover to Redwood Private (edge -> onprem) at 02:30 PST this morning. Since then we are seeing: 
- Multipart file uploads failing (4xx/5xx) for files > ~1400 bytes; smaller uploads succeed.
- Intermittent 502/504s from the app (frontend -> backend).
- Traceroutes show a hop where packets stop responding for larger MTU sizes.

Attached a short pcap and tcpdump from one of our load generators (capture-pcap-20261220.pcap).

Quick facts: our on-prem firewall preserves DF; we rely on PMTU. We suspect either: MTU blackhole on an interconnect, or ICMP "fragmentation needed" being dropped somewhere. We also saw many SYN retries in the capture.

Can you help triage? We can provide more traces or open a maintenance window. This is impacting several customers.

Thanks,
Nora Singh
Network Ops, AcmeTech
"Nora Singh" <nora@acmetech.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet failures after private cutover

Nora — thanks for the quick report and the pcap. I’ve looped in our networking on-call (Karthik) and edge ops (Vanessa).

Immediate asks so we can triage quickly:
1) Can you share a short traceroute (UDP and TCP) from the load generator to the Redwood edge and a reverse traceroute from the edge to your on-prem?
2) Can you confirm whether ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) appears in your capture?
3) Any recent firewall or transit ACL changes on your side?

Workarounds we can try quickly:
- Add a temporary MSS clamp at the edge or client side (~1400) to avoid DF-related blackholes.
- Temporarily allow ICMP frag-needed through your edge firewall if it is being blocked.

I’ll start a packet-path validation from the Redwood side and post findings here. If this is widespread we’ll propose an emergency maintenance window to apply a conservative MSS clamp on the edge.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora@acmetech.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet failures after private cutover

Quick initial analysis after looking at the pcap and our edge egress traces: 
- The pcap shows TCP segments with DF set and ICMP type 3 / code 4 responses originating from one of the intermediate transit routers. However the capture also shows those ICMP messages are *not* being delivered back to the originating host consistently. That matches a PMTU discovery failure.
- On our edge we also see SYN/ACKs being retransmitted and a noticeable number of RSTs when the backend tries to send larger packets.
- Additionally, I see our edge SNAT table is experiencing short bursts of high ephemeral allocation when the test generator opens many parallel connections. Under those bursts we hit ephemeral port reuse and some sessions are being torn when 5-tuple collision occurs (observed in conntrack logs).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk):
1) Add MSS clamp (1452 -> start 1400) on the Redwood edge for traffic to AcmeTech prefix. This avoids DF/fragmentation.
2) Adjust conntrack limits temporarily: increase nf_conntrack_max on the edge NAT boxes to 262144 and adjust timeouts for short-lived client connections.
3) Add/verify egress security group to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 from transit devices back to origin for PMTU discovery.

MSS clamp + allowed ICMP should restore flows. The conntrack bump prevents port exhaustion during peak parallel tests but is transient until we confirm steady state. We should schedule a controlled change window to make conntrack persistent and to review potential asymmetric return path issues with the transit provider (I’ll open a ticket).

I’ll kick off a targeted tcpdump and share immediate evidence.

— Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Singh <nora@acmetech.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet failures after private cutover

Update from ops after running a focused capture on the peering interface and edge router: 
- I confirmed ICMP type 3 code 4 packets are being generated by an upstream transit router (timestamped at 15:02:12 UTC).
- We do not see the corresponding ICMP returning to the origin IP because our egress security group rules were set to deny ICMP by default post-cutover; that denies PMTU signals.
- I temporarily added an egress rule to allow ICMP frag-needed (type 3 code 4) from the transit range, and started mirroring traffic for further analysis. After the rule the number of large-packet failures dropped substantially on my synthetic tests but not entirely — there remain sporadic multipart upload failures.
- I also observed asymmetric return path: some return traffic traverses a different transit provider where the SNAT mapping is different (edge SNAT -> different public IP), which could explain session mismatches when conntrack entries time out or collide.

Next steps I took:
- Allowed ICMP frag-needed in egress SG (temporary).
- Applied an MSS clamp on the test path (edge) with 1400 to validate behavior; tests show >85% success rate now.
- Captured a new pcap (attached) and uploaded a short runbook note to our Drive: runbook-private-cutover.md.

I recommend a follow-up change window to: 
1) Make egress ICMP PMTU exceptions permanent for the transit prefixes (with narrow source ranges).
2) Implement MSS clamp at the ASN-edge for AcmeTech prefixes.
3) Increase conntrack table and tune timeouts permanently, and coordinate with transit provider to normalize return-path SNAT.

— Vanessa
Edge Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
